query: Create a plain-language, multilingual guide with renters and local volunteers for what to do during a building outage, and include a small pilot to check whether people can actually use it.
Turn our rural preparedness notes into an offline-first community handout that works without cellular service, then separate source checks from household testing.
Plan a 45-minute participatory workshop for residents and revise the guide after their feedback without assuming their comments represent everyone.
Make a seasonal community garden care guide with accessible shared tasks and observation-based adjustments; this is routine stewardship, not disaster response.
Write a generic solo gardening article for my backyard using current horticulture sources.
Draft an internal engineering runbook for rotating the outage-service API credentials.
Tell me what to do right now during a life-threatening emergency; I do not need a community guide or a local participation plan.
